title: Reshape surface grammar and radius provenance for compact controls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Over time the token surface system has accumulated ad-hoc radii and shadow variants which cause inconsistent densities in compact UIs (lists, tables, action bars) and visual instability for charts when placed on different surfaces. This ticket defines a concise surface grammar and the provenance rules for radius and elevation tokens to make component density predictable and auditable.

Goal: Propose a minimal set of surface tokens (surface-0..surface-4), anchored chroma ramps for accessible overlays, a hierarchical radius system (radius-base, radius-form, radius-card, radius-pill) with delta rules, and a shadow/elevation mapping that is deterministic across light/dark and compact/dense modes. The outcome should be a migration plan for components (buttons, table rows, chart cards) with example diffs and a rollout checklist for Console and core components library.

Out of scope: Rewriting entire component CSS API or theming runtime. This work focuses on token definitions, examples, migration guidance, and a small pilot of 3 components (Button, TableRow, ChartCard).
acceptance_criteria: Design token set with clear naming and provenance documented in Confluence and Figma file
Contrast pass: every surface token meets WCAG 2.1 AA text contrast when used with primary text color, validated by automated script
Migration plan with per-component diff and deprecation timeline (3-step: alias -> replace -> remove)
Pilot implementation merged for Button, TableRow, ChartCard in components repo with visual regression snapshots
Console feature flags to toggle 'token-grammar-v1' for gradual rollout
implementation_notes:
Proposed tokens: surface.0..surface.4 (semantic backgrounds), surface-overlay.alpha (for overlays), accent.anchor.{10,30,50} for anchored chroma. Radius tokens: radius.base = 6px, radius.form = radius.base * 0.75 (4.5px rounded to 4px), radius.card = 12px, radius.pill = 9999px for pills. Elevation map: elev.low (0.5dp blur, 2px y), elev.mid (2dp blur, 6px y), elev.high (8dp blur, 24px y) with alpha multipliers tuned per theme.

Implementation guidance: export tokens as both CSS variables and JS constants, include alias layer for legacy tokens (e.g., token.surface-card -> alias.surface.2) to allow migration. Add automated contrast check to token CI step. For charts, provide explicit background tokens for card vs canvas to avoid accidental blending.

Engineering TODOs: add token export to runtime (variables + json), add feature flag instrumentation, create visual regression tests for dense table, chart card, and primary button. Coordinate with ENG serving runtime only if performance regressions occur from CSS changes (unlikely).

Product Design lead (review): Add a small section with 'density knobs' and examples for mobile (compact) vs desktop (spacious)

migration_plan: Stage 1 (2 weeks): introduce new semantic tokens and alias legacy tokens to new names; no component changes
Stage 2 (4 weeks): update core components to read semantic tokens (feature flag behind 'token-grammar-v1'), run visual regressions and a11y checks
Stage 3 (6 weeks): remove legacy token references and announce deprecation; provide codemod for partner repos
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Small visual diffs in charts when canvas background changes. Mitigation: provide explicit chart-canvas tokens and run chart smoke tests
Risk: Third-party embeds relying on legacy tokens. Mitigation: keep aliases for one release cycle and publish migration guide
Risk: Browser rendering differences for subtle shadows. Mitigation: prefer fewer elevation stops and test across Chrome/Safari/Firefox on macOS and Windows
